conventions.convention: Gaussian channels assume AC, finite dimension d ≥ 1, positive-definite noise covariance, fresh independent noise at each use, squared Euclidean input cost, and rates in nats per vector use.

Gaussian feedback encoders and decoders are Borel measurable; encoders use only the message and past outputs. Power is expected energy averaged over channel uses. Achievability requires codes for all sufficiently large blocklengths, vanishing average error, and the stated limiting inferior rate.
Finite DMC letter costs are finite nonnegative real numbers, and feasible budgets include the endpoint Γ = c_min.
Ordinary DMC codes are deterministic with equiprobable messages; cost is averaged over messages and coordinates, error is average error, and rates use natural logarithms.
DMC feedback encoders are causal deterministic maps, and feasibility uses expected average letter cost over the uniform message and channel outputs.

The countable-input model uses positive integer input labels, finite output alphabet, zero cost and budget, and information capacity defined as a supremum; no operational-capacity equality or attainment is asserted.
Water-filling uses positive noise variances, p_j = (T − λ_j)^+, and a uniquely determined water level only when P > 0; P = 0 is handled separately.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite DMC with finite nonnegative letter cost and Γ ≥ c_min, the feasible input set is nonempty and compact, C_I(Γ) is attained, 0 ≤ C_I(Γ) ≤ ln|X|, and C_I is nondecreasing and concave. At budgets above c_min, maximizing laws can be approximated by strictly feasible laws.

For positive λ_j and P ≥ 0, the maximum of one half the sum of ln(1 + p_j/λ_j) over nonnegative allocations summing to at most P is attained by water-filling; its value function is nondecreasing and concave.

If the expected fraction q_n of over-budget codewords and ensemble average error a_n satisfy q_n + a_n < 1, a deterministic subcode retains at least M(1 − √(q_n + a_n)) messages, has every retained word feasible, and has average error at most √(q_n + a_n)/(1 − √(q_n + a_n)). When q_n + a_n tends to zero, its rate loss tends to zero.

For a memoryless channel with a measurable density against a sigma-finite output reference measure, the IID ensemble expected average error is at most Pr[imath(X^n;Y^n) ≤ ln(M − 1) + τ] + exp(−τ), for n ≥ 1, M ≥ 2, and τ > 0; some deterministic code achieves this bound.
Let f:[a,∞)→R be finite and concave. If U is integrable, U ≥ a almost surely, and f(U) is integrable, then E f(U) ≤ f(E U).
Under AC, an independent finite-support vector input with E||X||² ≤ P into independent positive-variance Gaussian branches satisfies I(X;X+Z) ≤ C_d(P), the water-filling allocation maximum.
For a uniform N-message variable, N ≥ 2, observed through conditional densities and a measurable decoder of error e, H(M|Y) ≤ H(M|g(Y)) ≤ h_2(e) + e ln(N − 1) ≤ ln 2 + e ln N.
Finite-alphabet entropy with 0 ln 0 = 0 is continuous and concave on the probability simplex and satisfies 0 ≤ H(p) ≤ ln m.
